note: Hebrew yaskil (Hiphil of sakal) can mean "act prudently" or "prosper, succeed"; in a military context, and given Yahweh "with him" (v. 14), success is the likelier sense (same verb in vv. 14, 15, 30).

kjv: he (Saul) prophesied in the midst of the house
note: Hebrew vayyitnabbe' (Hithpael of naba') covers ecstatic, uncontrolled behaviour; under an evil spirit it describes frenzy rather than prophecy in the usual sense.

kjv: Thou (David) shalt this day be my son in law in [the one of] the twain
mine: You (David) shall now be my son-in-law a second time
note: Hebrew bishtayim titchatten bi ha-yom is obscure; it is most likely "a second time" (after the failed Merab offer), while the KJV supplies words to make it "by one of the two daughters".
Hebrew mohar is the payment the groom makes to the bride's father; a "dowry" in modern usage is property the bride's family gives, the reverse direction.
